Volvo Cars and NVIDIA Expand Partnership to Advance Safe Automated Driving

cards.body: Volvo Cars today announced it is expanding its partnership with NVIDIA to unlock new levels of safety in automated driving technology in future cars from Volvo, building on the companies’ decade-long collaboration. Guided by Volvo Cars’ pioneering safety knowledge and powered by the NVIDIA Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, the technology will enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door. This includes everything from highways and busy urban streets to parking scenarios. The technology will make its debut in a next-generation Volvo car as part of the company’s recently announced largest-ever product push. Volvo Cars will combine its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with NVIDIA’s AI and accelerated computing technologies. These include the Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, Halos OS, and Alpamayo Stack driving software. Together, the companies will raise the bar for AI-enabled car safety while making driving feel easier and more effortless for customers, with a gradual introduction of eyes-off and mind-off driving. Volvo Cars brings nearly a century of real-world safety research and its human-centric approach to this development. The ambition is to set a new benchmark for automated driving that is safe, convenient and worthy of customer trust. “Volvo has been synonymous with car safety for almost 100 years,” said Håkan Samuelsson, president and CEO of Volvo Cars. “By working with NVIDIA, we bring together two distinct strengths: industry-leading safety knowledge and world-class AI technology. That combination gives us a unique opportunity to create safer and more attractive cars for our customers.” “Accelerated computing has transformed the car into an intelligent machine that can understand the world around it,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Volvo has spent nearly a century protecting people on the road. Together, we’re combining Volvo’s extraordinary vehicle safety systems with NVIDIA Hyperion and Halos to build a new generation of cars that make driving safer and more effortless.” This expanded partnership marks another milestone in the companies’ long-standing collaboration, which began in 2017. Volvo Cars is bringing the industry’s most advanced computing capabilities into its next generation of electric cars, establishing it as a leader in software-defined cars.

Volvo makes a bigger bet on Nvidia for hands-free automated driving

cards.body: Volvo is leveling up its automated driving system through an expansion of its nearly decade-long partnership with Nvidia. The companies announced on Thursday that Volvo will use three pieces of Nvidia hardware and software in its future vehicles to provide an automated driving system that can navigate urban streets and highways. Under the expanded partnership, Volvo will combine its vehicle safety systems and engineering with Nvidia’s Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, Alpamayo driving software stack, and Halos safety evaluation layer. The Alpamayo stack is redundant and diverse, according to Ali Kani, who heads up Nvidia’s automotive division. It combines Alpamayo, a family of AI models, datasets, and simulation and development tools used to build autonomous-driving software, with classical software that uses machine learning and camera and radar perception, he said. “The point is we run these two stacks at the same time, and we have multimodal sensors in our philosophy because it’s a safer product that way,” Kani said, adding that the open source Alpamayo software has now been downloaded by more than 650,000 developers. Volvo didn’t reveal the value of the partnership or which vehicle model would be the first to use this new Nvidia tech stack. But Alwin Bakkenes, Volvo’s head of software development, hinted at the scale of the deal and how it represents the automaker’s evolution toward developing a full-tech stack designed for its electric vehicles as well as its plug-in hybrids and gas-powered vehicles. “Automakers used to be very much like car-line-based development and working with various suppliers, etc. and we have completely changed and migrated into being a full-tech stack company,” Bakkenes said, adding that Volvo will start this partnership with a brand new vehicle that “will come in the not-too-near future.” He said the first vehicle with this new Nvidia tech stack will debut within the decade, and “then of course the technology can go beyond that.” While Volvo’s relationship with Nvidia isn’t new, the expanded partnership represents the automaker’s effort to bring the latest automated driving software to all of its vehicles — not just its EVs. All of Volvo’s battery-electric vehicles use Nvidia’s Orin computer chip, which processes information from cameras, radar, and other sensors to help a vehicle understand its surroundings and make driving decisions. “What we’re going to do in the future is actually standardize more on Hyperion — also from a sensor set perspective — to really open up the stack for the wider partnership with Nvidia,” Bakkenes said.

cards.body: NVIDIA today released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter model that delivers the fastest task completion and highest accuracy for specialized always-on agents. Joining it are two new edge models: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, optimized to balance intelligence and speed per GB for local agentic workloads, and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, optimized for intelligence per GB for fast conversational agents. Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B are available now, with Bolt E4B coming Oct. 23. The three open models together cover the full range of agent deployments, from large enterprise servers down to edge devices and local hardware. Any organization that wants to run agents on NVIDIA infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier, without having to choose between capability and deployability. Super VL and Bolt join the Nemotron family alongside Lightning and Ultra. Lightning, released in August, handles high-throughput workloads; Ultra handles the hardest reasoning tasks; and Bolt brings intelligence to the edge. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: Frontier Accuracy at One-Fifth the Size Super VL, built in collaboration with the Nemotron Coalition , delivers leading accuracy on multimodal agentic tasks — instruction following, tool use, multistep business workflows, and visual understanding — comparable with NVIDIA’s largest reasoning model at roughly one-fifth the parameter count. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL delivers frontier-level intelligence in its class for high-volume agentic workflows. As the fastest open agentic model in its class — 5x faster than the next best — it helps enterprise agents complete high-volume tasks faster across workflows that span days or weeks. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index leadboard, achieves up to 5x faster throughput compared to other models in its class. Unlike closed frontier models, organizations can post-train Super VL on their own data, deploy it on their own infrastructure and oversee what they build. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt: Agentic Intelligence at the Edge Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run everyday agentic tasks locally on NVIDIA RTX/DGX Spark, using a native 2-bit quantization to fit in 24GB of memory and run alongside other applications. Relative to other models with a similar memory footprint, it provides a good balance of intelligence and speed: smart enough to get most jobs done, yet much faster than the smartest models. With Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, users can delegate their projects to popular local agent harnesses — from researching the web to writing to debugging code — all without sending those workloads to the cloud. It is the #1 open model in its class on PinchBench , and the #2 open model for BrowseComp . Bolt E4B 4GB is built for physical and conversational agents on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. cards.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced the RTX Spark platform with the grand ambition to “reinvent the PC” back at Computex 2026. By pairing the GB10 Superchip with a version of Windows on Arm tailored for the secure and contained execution of local AI agents, Nvidia and its partners at Microsoft, Dell, HP, MSI, Lenovo, and Asus are all hoping to pave the way to a future where the PC is an active, autonomous companion for work and creation. The hardware foundation for that vision of the future is now in place. Last week, we flew out to San Francisco to get all the details on the RTX Spark platform, and we returned home with Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra in top-end trim to put it all to the test. This system has the full RTX Spark Superchip with 20 CPU cores and 6144 CUDA cores alongside 128GB of LPDDR5X-9400 RAM, and I’ve been putting it through its paces over the past week to see just what it can do. The embargoes for the RTX Spark launch are a bit peculiar. Today, we’ll be sharing our broad experience with the Spark platform, as well as competitive performance evaluations, but not any system-specific results such as battery life, build or display quality, or other details of that nature. We have other RTX Spark laptops in the Tom’s Hardware labs, and detailed reviews of those systems will be coming soon. No, this approach doesn’t make a lot of sense when the experience of a mobile platform is intimately and inextricably tied to the specific implementation of that chip in a particular laptop design. And we know that battery life is the first and foremost concern of many interested in this platform. But again, all that information is coming soon. For this first round of testing, we compared the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark against two systems. The first is a 14" MacBook Pro with Apple's highest-end M5 Max SoC inside. That Mac has a 40-core GPU and an 18-core CPU, as well as 128 GB of LPDDR5X RAM. We don't have a mobile Ryzen AI Max+ 395 system in the labs right now, but we do have AMD's compact Ryzen AI Halo as a source of fresh data with the latest ROCm stack and llama.cpp builds. Local AI performance Judging local AI performance is a constantly moving target, and this review is no different. Our past testing has exercised the prompt processing and token generation phases of AI inference separately, with the understanding that a system that's fast at both those phases provides the best experience. headlines.body: As Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.'s record quarter makes clear, demand from chipmakers shows no sign of slowing down. In fact, TSMC can't manufacture quickly enough. The artificial intelligence boom has created unending need for space on factory lines at the world's leading chip manufacturer, and it could put a chokehold on the entire industry's ability to scale. Last year, TSMC said it had the capacity to make more than 17 million 12-inch equivalent wafers. But customers want more. "The competition is extremely fierce," said Jordan Klein, an analyst at Mizuho Securities. "It's a game of who can get the most leverage and supply." TSMC makes the vast majority of the world's most advanced semiconductors, the graphics processors and central processors from Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom that are necessary for running AI workloads. Now a growing number of tech firms – Apple, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and OpenAI – also rely on TSMC to make custom in-house AI accelerators. TSMC North American CEO Sajiv Dalal told CNBC he gets at least 10 calls a day about wafer capacity. TSMC posted record profit for a sixth straight quarter on Thursday and expects fourth-quarter revenue to be 58% higher than a year earlier, driven by strong demand for its advanced chipmaking technologies. If compute demand continues to grow at the current rate over the next 12 to 18 months, Klein said capacity constraints at TSMC could threaten some of the industry's massive infrastructure investments and the "aggressive revenue growth targets" from the AI companies. U.S. hyperscalers are projecting well over $700 billion in capital expenditures this year, and analysts expect that figure to jump in 2027. AI ambitions are also threatened by a global shortage of memory chips. The logic chips that TSMC manufactures are more complex and expensive to produce. That means GPU and CPU leaders like Nvidia and AMD work out lengthy contracts and bespoke deals with TSMC behind closed doors years in advance. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD CEO Lisa Su have both visited Taiwan multiple times this year. Sid Sheth, CEO of AI chip startup D-Matrix, has fostered a relationship with TSMC for more than 20 years, and his company relies on TSMC to manufacture its processors. For TSMC customers, many roads lead to Kevin Zhang, a senior vice president of the Taiwanese company and a central figure in determining which chipmakers get access to its coveted factory lines. He's "currently probably the most popular person on the planet," Sheth said in an interview. Sheth said that Jerry Qubain, D-Matrix's vice president of manufacturing, has been visiting TSMC since 1992 and goes to Taiwan three to four times a year. "This was even before Nvidia was founded," Sheth said. "That's a good example of a person we brought on board because of the relationships he has at TSMC." Qubain joined D-Matrix in 2024. headlines.body: NTT Global Data Centres has deployed an Nvidia GPU cluster at its Munich 2 data center. According to the company, the cluster provides clients with a “real-world environment” where they can test how their AI applications will perform at scale before investing in broad deployments themselves. Unlike a traditional AI demonstration or innovation lab, the cluster – which NTT has dubbed AI Factory Munich – allows customers to evaluate AI workloads against the infrastructure, security, data, governance and operational requirements they will face in production. In a post on LinkedIn, Anne-Sophie Lotgering, CEO Europe, NTT, said that Nvidia and Dell provided the infrastructure whilst Red Hat and Mistral AI worked with the company on the platform and the model. The cluster is comprised of Nvidia Blackwell GPUs interconnected via Nvidia Spectrum-X Ethernet technology, with servers and storage provided by Dell’s AI Factory, with Nvidia offering. “Every leader I speak to wants AI they own, control and trust. At NTT Data's AI factory Munich, they can run their own applications and data in a production data center, on their terms, before they commit to deployment. It‘s the difference between a slide and a decision,” said Graham Clarke, managing director, global private and sovereign AI, NTT Data. Located in the German town of Unterschleißheim outside Munich, Bavaria, NTT’s 6,300 sqm (67,813 sq ft) Munich 2 campus consists of two buildings offering 14MW of critical IT load.

headlines.body: AI 추천 뉴스 베슬AI "2030년까지 GPU 20만개 확보" 네오클라우드 사업 전략 발표 안재만 대표 "GPU금융 2조로" “2030년까지 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 20만개를 확보하겠습니다.” 안재만 베슬AI 대표는 15일 서울 드림플러스 강남에서 열린 ‘2026 네오클라우드 전략 발표회’에서 이같이 말했다. 네오클라우드는 인공지능(AI) 기업이 값비싼 GPU를 직접 구매하지 않고도 AI 모델을 개발하고 운영할 수 있도록 컴퓨팅 자원을 빌려주는 서비스다. 2020년 설립된 베슬AI는 GPU 관리 소프트웨어 개발에서 출발해 네오클라우드 사업으로 영역을 넓히고 있다. 업스테이지 등 국내외 AI 기업에 서비스를 제공 중이다. 베슬AI는 현재 약 7000개인 GPU를 올해 말 1만개, 내년 5만개, 2030년 20만개까지 늘리겠다고 강조했다. 안 대표는 “2028년까지 500MW 정도의 데이터센터를 확보할 계획”이라며 전국 8곳에 AI 데이터센터 거점을 마련한다는 구상을 밝혔다. GPU 확보에 필요한 자금은 금융사와의 협력 및 외부 투자 유치로 마련한다. 현재 4000억원 규모의 GPU 금융을 추진 중이며, 내년에는 2조원 규모로 확대할 계획이다. 안 대표는 “글로벌 투자은행들과 수 조원 단위의 GPU 금융을 협의하고 있다”고 말했다. 베슬AI의 올해 상반기 매출은 약 1300억원이다. 안 대표는 연간 매출로 2500억원을 제시하면서 “내년에는 7000억원, 2028년에는 2조원 이상으로 늘리겠다”고 강조했다. 이어 “베슬AI는 리벨리온, 퓨리오사AI 등 국내 반도체 기업과 협력해 국산 신경망처리장치(NPU)를 활용한 AI 인프라도 구축할 예정”이라며 “내년 상반기에는 엔비디아의 차세대 GPU인 베라 루빈 기반 클러스터를 도입할 계획”이라고 덧붙였다. 유지희 기자 keephee@hankyung.com

summary_data.why_matters: 북유럽은 재생에너지, 데이터 거버넌스, 학계-산업 연계라는 구조적 강점을 바탕으로 **유럽 내 AI 인프라 허브로 빠르게 성장**하고 있으며, 이는 NVIDIA의 유럽 시장 확장 전략에 중요한 거점이 된다. 동시에 다수의 클라우드 공급업체와 스타트업이 NVIDIA 생태계(Nemotron, DGX, Omniverse 등)에 집중되는 현상은 지역 차원의 플랫폼 종속을 심화시킨다.
summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 투자·인프라 공급·오픈모델(Nemotron) 제공을 결합해 **북유럽을 자사 AI 스택의 쇼케이스 지역으로 삼아** 유럽 전반의 소버린 AI·클라우드 전략에서 영향력을 확대하고 있다.
summary_data.focus_angle: ABB Robotics는 NVIDIA Omniverse 기반 RobotStudio HyperReality로 로봇 시뮬레이션 정확도 최대 99%, 커미셔닝 시간 최대 80% 단축을 달성해 **산업용 로봇 디지털 트윈 분야에서 NVIDIA 플랫폼의 실질적 적용 사례**를 보여준다.

headlines.body: The Nordic countries have become the European leader in unicorn startup density, producing the most emerging companies valued at $1 billion or more per capita on the continent. Now, a new chapter for the region is unfolding as countries race to build one of Europe’s most consequential technology ecosystems. The many computing advancements already underway in the Nordics, combined with the opportunity that lies ahead, signal a region moving from ambition to application. NVIDIA’s Investments in the Nordics Over the past year, NVIDIA has invested in the technology ecosystem in the Nordics, including Sweden’s leading startups Lovable and Legora. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Lovable , a Stockholm-based startup, provides a software creation platform that enables anyone to build and run software using plain language. In collaboration with NVIDIA, Lovable is optimizing inference for open models and training its models using NVIDIA Dynamo software and Nemotron tools. Legora provides an agentic operating system for legal work, supporting lawyers in research, review and drafting across complex matters. Nordics Emerge as Infrastructure Hub The foundation for establishing the Nordics as a technology powerhouse is already being built and the region holds a structural advantage: abundant renewable energy, rigorous data governance and a research tradition that bridges academia and industry. The Nordics are one of Europe’s fastest growing hubs for infrastructure. AI clouds are expanding with a projected 1 gigawatts of capacity to be deployed across the region by the end of 2027. Among these cloud providers are Bitdeer, CoreWeave , Crusoe , Hyperstack, Nscale , Verda and Volta . In Sweden, a consortium anchored by Ericsson, AstraZeneca, Saab, SEB and Wallenberg Investments, with SKF as strategic partner, launched Sferical One — a shared supercomputer running on two NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs with 16 racks of NVIDIA DGX GB300 systems and 1,152 GPUs. The consortium will build services using NVIDIA Nemotron open models, which allow researchers to customize and deploy their models in a secure environment. Nordic-Built Intelligence Some of the Nordics’ leading technology companies are now building proprietary intelligence on NVIDIA infrastructure. Spotify , which personalizes music, podcasts and audiobooks for hundreds of millions of listeners, uses NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM inference software to run AI-powered podcast recommendations faster and cheaper at scale. The deployment is a case study in inference efficiency: delivering the same recommendations to a global audience at a lower cost per query. ABB Robotics developed RobotStudio HyperReality using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to bridge the gap between robot simulations and real-world performance. headlines.body: Much of today’s scientific progress begins with computation. But turning accelerated computing’s potential into scientific progress — modeling climate systems, designing molecules, simulating materials and more — depends on more than breakthrough technology. Especially for smaller labs, early-career scientists or science-based startups, the hardest part of research can be everything that comes before the science: assembling tools, finding compute and building the expertise to use both. At the AI in Science Summit in Dublin today, the European Commission launched the AI in Science Enablers Initiative, a shared framework connected to RAISE — the Resource for AI Science in Europe — that brings private-sector support closer to Europe’s research community. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements NVIDIA is joining the campaign , providing: Access to accelerated tools, models and platforms Compute, cloud resources, data and scientific resources Skills, training and technical support Collaborative projects and pilots along with support for researchers and talent Support for startups and ecosystem development “Europe’s ambition in AI in science can only become reality if we bring together the strengths of our research community, industry and other partners,” Ekaterina Zaharieva, European Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation. “Through the AI in Science Enablers campaign, we are turning this ambition into concrete commitments that give researchers access to the tools, expertise and resources they need to innovate.” Open Models NVIDIA’s pledge begins with open source technology. NVIDIA has released more than 250 open models, 250 open datasets and over 1,400 open source software projects spanning large language models, healthcare, robotics, climate science, physical AI, autonomous vehicles and scientific research. The models and datasets are available on Hugging Face and GitHub. Building on this open ecosystem, researchers can build agentic reasoning capabilities with NVIDIA Nemotron — a family of architectures, open weights, open source models, training data and recipes — and scientific software including NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit , NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo libraries, NVIDIA Earth-2 models and NVIDIA ALCHEMI NIM microservices to accelerate research across biology, chemistry, molecular design, weather and climate, energy, engineering, physics and material sciences. Skills and Training Building advanced intelligence capability across Europe requires knowledge that travels as freely as compute. The NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute has launched a new open source courseware hub with hands-on course materials covering accelerated computing and deep learning — freely downloadable and openly licensed, with no enrollment, fees or deadline. Modular by design, the courses can be adapted for university curricula, supercomputing center bootcamps or developer community events, and serve as a direct bridge to NVIDIA’s broader training and certification programs .

headlines.body: ASML has said that the unprecedented spending and investment brought about by the artificial intelligence (AI) boom is not slowing down at all, as customers are already lining up to place orders for its advanced chipmaking tools for 2029 and 2030, according to a Reuters report citing ASML's Q3 2026 earnings published today, October 14. ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet said that the company would struggle to meet the demand despite plans announced in July to raise capacity by 30% in 2027 and another 30% in 2028. The company also confirmed on Wednesday that it will raise prices starting in 2027, with the full effect showing in 2028. It projects Q4 sales of €14.2 billion to €15.2 billion ($15.9 billion to $17 billion), boosting its full-year sales projections from at least €43 billion to €44-45 billion. ASML's shares rose 2% on Wednesday, up almost 70% so far this year, with its €586 billion market valuation making it Europe's largest firm by market cap. According to Reuters , there had been concerns that the AI investment boom was losing steam. However, positive projections from the largest manufacturer of the tools for making AI chips and advanced semiconductors signal that chipmakers will keep expanding, sustaining demand across the AI industry well into the foreseeable future. "There were concerns that the AI trade was running out of steam," Gordon Kerr, European macro strategist at KBRA, said. "Demand for chips remains strong, and infrastructure spending is likely to continue well into 2027." ASML's customers include logic chip manufacturers such as Samsung, Intel, and TSMC, which manufactures chips for Nvidia, all of whom are heavily investing in increasing chip production . Memory chip makers SK Hynix and Micron ⁠have also announced expansion plans that involve ASML machines. Meanwhile, the company's CFO Roger Dassen said it is "still kicking the tires on the exact size of that (Terafab) opportunity," referring to Elon Musk's 100 million square feet semiconductor manufacturing facility that aims to output millions of logic and memory chips. Boltz, a London-based AI startup founded by MIT researchers, builds biomolecular models and AI agents that help scientists predict molecular structures and interactions, and design potential new medicines. Foresight, a London-based startup, helps owners of major infrastructure projects, including hyperscale data centers, predict completion dates, mitigate risks and accelerate time to revenue. Hiverge, a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning. Prima Mente, a London-based AI biology startup, focuses on building biological foundation models to decode complex diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets, starting with Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and ALS. Riverlane, a Cambridge-based quantum computing startup, builds real-time error correction hardware and software that work across all major qubit types, helping quantum computers become reliable enough for practical use. Sign-ups are open now on Sipeed’s MaixStation page ahead of a Kickstarter campaign at the end of the year, with units shipping within three months after it closes. headlines.body: 스카이월드와이드와 계열사 스카이인텔리전스가 정부의 피지컬 인공지능(AI) 산업 육성을 위한 민관 협력체인 ‘피지컬 AI 얼라이언스’에 참여한다. 양사는 각각 데이터 기술과 글로벌 제조 협력 분야에서 활동할 계획이다. 15일 스카이월드와이드에 따르면 회사는 피지컬 AI 얼라이언스의 ‘K-피지컬 AI 풀스택 분과’ 데이터 액션그룹에 참여한다. 스카이인텔리전스는 ‘기반 거버넌스 분과’ 글로벌 협력 액션그룹에 참여한다. 피지컬 AI 얼라이언스는 국내 피지컬 AI 기술 개발과 산업 적용을 지원하는 민관 협력체다. 얼라이언스는 핵심 기술 확보를 담당하는 ‘K-피지컬 AI 풀스택 분과’와 산업별 적용을 추진하는 ‘버티컬 산업 브릿지 분과’로 구성된다. 표준·신뢰·인재·국제 협력 등을 다루는 ‘기반 거버넌스 분과’도 운영한다. 정부는 2027년 피지컬 AI 관련 예산안을 올해 9000억원에서 3조1000억원으로 늘려 편성했다. 정부는 기술 개발과 학습 인프라 구축 및 현장 실증 지원을 확대할 계획이다. 양사는 지난 13~14일 서울 코엑스에서 열린 ‘피지컬 AI Tech Week’에서 기술과 협력 계획을 소개했다. 신재혁 스카이월드와이드 대표와 한동균 스카이인텔리전스 사업부장은 한국지능정보사회진흥원(NIA)과 KAIST가 주관한 기반 거버넌스 분과 행사에서 각각 발표했다. 스카이월드와이드는 자체 그래프 데이터베이스(DB) 기술을 활용해 기업 데이터를 AI가 활용할 수 있는 지식으로 전환하는 역할을 맡는다. 회사는 공공·금융·제조 분야의 고객사 130곳 이상을 대상으로 사업 337건을 수행했다고 설명했다. 스카이인텔리전스는 산업용 로봇 기업 ABB 로보틱스와 진행한 정밀 합성데이터 검증 경험을 활용할 계획이다. 회사는 ABB 로보틱스·엔비디아 공동 백서에 주요 기여자로 참여한 경험을 토대로 국내 기업 및 연구기관과 AI 학습·검증 사례를 공유할 예정이다. 신재혁 스카이월드와이드 대표는 “데이터 활용과 학습·검증 분야의 협력을 확대해 실제 산업 현장에서 성과를 내도록 지원하겠다”고 말했다. 한동균 스카이인텔리전스 사업부장은 “다양한 제조 조건을 정밀하게 학습 데이터에 반영하는 것이 핵심”이라며 “글로벌 검증 경험을 AI 학습 자산으로 축적해 국내 기업·연구기관의 현장 적용을 뒷받침하겠다”고 밝혔다. 박혜원 기자 sunone@chosunbiz.com
